newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Zedillo pledges no mercy on drugs, crime.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Zedillo pledges no mercy on drugs, crime.

text.p: With pressure mounting from the United States, Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo lashed out at high-level government corruption on Wednesday and pledged no mercy in the fight against drugs and crime.
"We must establish, clearly, the notion that in our country there should not and cannot be anyone untouchable," Zedillo said in a speech to Mexico's Jewish community.
"I am absolutely determined and committed to work to the end of my abilities, to the last drop of my energy to deal with this problem," he said.
Calling on Mexicans to become "intolerant of law-breaking," Zedillo dismissed "skeptics, cynics and those who rashly believe that we are not serious."

His remarks coincided with a fierce debate over whether President Bill Clinton should "certify" Mexico is cooperating with the United States in its fight against illegal drugs. He is required to make a decision by the end of the month.
Last week Mexico's antinarcotics czar Gen. Jesus Gutierrez Rebollo was fired and arrested on charges that he worked for Amado Carrillo Fuentes, the head of Mexico's most powerful drugs cartel.

The New York Times also published allegations this week that two Mexican state governors and the father, brother and late brother-in-law of ex-President Carlos Salinas de Gortari were all involved with drug-traffickers. The governors and the Salinas family have denied the allegations.
Zedillo made the remarks replying to complaints by Jewish community leaders about government corruption and high crime levels.

"We view with concern, impotence and annoyance how drug-trafficking continues to permeate our society ... reaching high levels of authority which we had believed incorruptible," community leader Alfredo Achar told Zedillo.
The Clinton administration will not decide whether to certify Mexico as an ally in the drug war until Friday at the earliest, the State Department said on Wednesday.
